title: Jail, the inquest and the accusation of drunkenness
summary: He is jailed overnight, the cab company's lawyers try to prove he was drunk, but the death is ruled accidental in his favour.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You were just in jail the rest of that night basically weren't you?
Yeah -- and, of course, that car was - oh, boy - the car was just totalled. And, then, of course, there was a trial---

An inquest-- it's an inquest actually- and, uh, I told my whole story and, of course, the cab company had a fleet of lawyers and I had one -- you know -- one that I couldn't even afford I had -- and, uh, they tried to say--- they tried to prove or say that I was drunk--
Yeah but for the cab company--
For the cab company -- which I wasn't.
And, we hadn't had a drink; we were just up there playing records and that kind of thing. So---
But, the police verified your story--- the police who investigated it---
Oh, yeah -- well, they smell your breath and they do all the things -- and those days, they didn't have balloons you blow up or anything but it was definitely found out that I was not drunk---
So, when the trial came up they tried, of course, to do all that and they said -- I didn't stop -- when I did stop -- and you know, they tried--- well, you know, the tricks of it---

What the lawyers were trying to do is not involve the cab company in the accident; they said it was my fault. He hit me - I didn't hit him; so it turned out that it was definitely established that it was an accidental death - an accidental death in my favor -- now, how the story got around - now this is only hear-say -- I can't say that this actually happened, but somebody started a rumor; somebody told me at that time that, uh, Mugsy, had made the crack some place along the line that -- I guess Davison was loaded or this wouldn't have happened--
